stem.en: A sealed packet of chips swells on the road from Delhi up to Leh. Why?

text.en: Less air lies above Leh, so the air outside presses in less.

feedback.en: Yes. The air inside now pushes out harder than the air outside pushes in.

text.en: More air lies above Leh, so the air outside presses in more.

feedback.en: Going up leaves less air above you, not more.

text.en: The chips give off gas on the journey.

feedback.en: The change comes from the air around the packet, and it reverses on the way down.

text.en: Outside air leaks into the sealed packet.

feedback.en: The packet is sealed, so the air in it stays the same.

explanation.en: Air pressure is the weight of the air above. Leh lies about 3,500 m up, so less air lies above it and pressure is lower. The air sealed inside the packet then pushes out harder than the outside air pushes in.

hints.en: What changes on the outside of the packet?
Is there more air above you in Delhi or at Leh?
